title: When to Remind Team Members They Are Part of Something Bigger Than Themselves
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note is about timing, not content: leaders should hold their 'bigger purpose' message in reserve and deploy it specifically at moments when they're asking team members to accept unpopular changes or short-term sacrifices. Reminding people of the collective purpose at exactly that moment reframes the ask and softens resistance more effectively than repeating the message constantly. The piece emphasizes that while keeping a larger vision visible is generally good practice, its persuasive power is greatest when saved for the moments people actually need perspective.
points: The 'you're part of something bigger' message is most persuasive when timed specifically to moments of sacrifice or change.
Constantly repeating a larger purpose is less impactful than deploying it strategically when needed.
Leaders must be able to precisely articulate why the larger vision matters, not just gesture at it.
This message is framed as reframing an ask rather than eliminating resistance to it outright.
The underlying goal is reminding team members that their sacrifice contributes to a collective, valued outcome.
quotes: Leaders often have to ask team members to sacrifice their self-interest or to accept uncomfortable changes.
While it is good practice to keep the larger purpose or vision that is bigger than any one person consistently in front of the team, it is during periods of change that it is most impactful.
The best leaders save the case for why everyone is a part of something bigger than themselves for when they must ask others to adopt unpopular changes or make short-term sacrifices.
Reminding team members about why they really work so hard and commit to overcoming difficult problems and situations softens any resistance to the need to change or sacrifice.
Greatness in all dimensions is born from sacrifice for the larger good.
